newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian army kills 100 rebels - paper.
newsitem.headline: Algerian army kills 100 rebels - paper.

text.p: Algerian soldiers have killed around 100 Moslem guerrillas and wiped out a main rebel rear base in a huge operation in the northeastern province of Tizi-Ouzou, the Algerian newspaper El Watan said on Thursday.
Helicopters and special airborne troops were used in the five-day operation in Sidi Ali Bounab forest near Tizi-Ouzou, 90 km (60 miles) east of Algiers.
El Watan, normally well-informed on security issues, said around 100 rebels were killed in the operation started last Saturday.

"It resulted in the destruction of numerous hideouts...a bomb-making factory and the discovery and destruction of a field hospital which served (the rebels) for the whole of the central region of the country," it said.
The hospital was built after 1990 when the now-outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) controlled the local regional authority, the newspaper added.
Algerian authorities replaced elected FIS-controlled local councils with government appointees after cancelling in January 1992 a general election in which the FIS had taken a commanding lead.
El Watan said the hospital served as the medical centre for the fundamentalist rebels for a vast region.

"The Sidi Ali Bounab underground was set up in the Afghan fashion: advance hideouts, fortified buried pillboxes, and real rear bases, the whole protected by a system of bomb boobytraps on all the roads and paths."

Earlier this week, El Watan said 20 guerrillas were killed in an initial sweep in the forest in the night between Saturday and Sunday, and that on Monday troops were besieging rebels holed up in a cave.
Algerian security forces have been out in force for the past few weeks, carrying out search operations against guerrillas ahead of the June 5 parliamentary elections.

Excluding the latest operation, more than 200 Moslem rebels have been killed in such sweeps, including some guerrilla leaders whose hideouts in Algiers were raided last month, according to Algerian newspaper reports.
About 60,000 people have been killed in Algeria's violence pitting government forces against Moslem guerrillas since early 1992.
